Azazel_2020-07-14_gcc13_x64_libselinux.s.build_flags: gcc -O0 (upstream sets no -O: Makefile CFLAGS is only -Wall, compile adds -g) -fPIC -shared -Wl,-soname,libselinux.so, linked -lc -ldl -lpam -lutil; this recipe adds -fcommon (GCC 10 made -fno-common the default and azazel.h:31 is a tentative definition in a header) and -D_STAT_VER=3 on x86 / 1 on x64 (glibc 2.33 removed __xstat and the _STAT_VER macro); upstream's trailing `strip libselinux.so` is not run
Azazel_2020-07-14_gcc13_x64_libselinux.s.notes: An LD_PRELOAD userland rootkit, linked as a shared object and installed by writing its path into /etc/ld.so.preload. Chronicle's Winnti-for-Linux reporting, via MITRE S0430, describes a modified copy shipped as libxselinux.so, one character off upstream's own -Wl,-soname,libselinux.so. Built WITHOUT -fvisibility=hidden, unlike every other ELF recipe here: an interposition library's exports are the artefact, and hiding open/__xstat/pam_authenticate would produce a shape upstream cannot build and no sample resembles; the unnamed .plt stubs in the reports are the cost. 56 symbol-carrying functions on x64 and 60 on x86, 30 exported on both, the x64 total summing over the objects as azazel 38, pam 7, crypthook 6, pcap 3, xor 2. make config is not run: upstream commits const.h, and it was verified to be config.py's own default output by decoding its syscall_table under config.py's xor (c ^ 0xfe), which returns the 24 names in config.py's order, so the string table is upstream's default configuration rather than one chosen here. Most of this family's functions are named after the libc and PAM entry points they hook, so it is the hardest test in the corpus of the rule that baseline.py drops a function only on symbol AND PicHash; the drop count here should be read with that in mind. crypthook.c is vendored from chokepoint/CryptHook (6 functions in the object) and stays under this family, being below the eight-function floor on its own. Upstream links no -lcrypto despite crypthook.c calling EVP_*, so the artefact carries 8 undefined OpenSSL references - upstream's shape, not an error here. Issue #55 asks that this be decided with Medusa (#40). Medusa is a userland LD_PRELOAD library, built separately in PR 102. At the ten-instruction PicHash floor, the committed x86/x64 family unions have 101 Azazel hashes and 146 Medusa hashes with zero shared hashes. Shared hook names do not establish identical implementations.
